To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a versatile encapsulation technology for micron-sized emulsion gels and capsules that is based on pH-responsive amphiphilic polymers.
the combination of pH-responsive polyelectrolys and surfactant-like side-chain groups enables the encapsulation of hydrophobic substances with a high degree of control over morphology and rheology.

the combination of the pH responsiveness, the viscoelastic properties, and the amphiphilicity of a comb copolymer allows the preparation of a versatile technology for the preparation of emulsion gels and capsules with a high degree of tunability of the morphology and rheology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of stimuli-responsive polymer systems.
the development of novel amphiphilic polymers for the preparation of functional emulsion gels and capsules.
the development of novel, versatile encapsulation methods based on stimuli-responsive polymers.

the presented method is a versatile technology for encapsulation of hydrophobic substances with a high degree of flexibility in the choice of the hydrophobe, the processing conditions, and the final product properties.

we have developed an encapsulation technology that allows the production of stable dispersions of emulsion gels and capsules with a hydrophobic substance as the liquid core, and the encapsulating polymer as the shell.
the presented technology is versatile, simple, and robust, and it can be used in a wide range of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a versatile method for the encapsulation of hydrophobic substances.
we have developed a versatile encapsulation technology that allows the preparation of micron-sized emulsion gels and capsules with high stability and a high degree of customization.
we have demonstrated a new technology that is able to produce stable dispersions of emulsion gels and capsules by the use of a single polymer and a one-pot process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of stimuli responsiveness, viscoelasticity, and interfacial activity provided by the amphiphilic copolymer enables the production of stable dispersions of micron-sized particles with a wide range of morphologies.

the encapsulation technology based on the pH-responsive amphiphilic polymers can be tailored to produce emulsions of various viscoelasticity and stability, as well as capsules of different morphology, depending on the composition and architecture of the side-chain surfactant.

the combination of a pH-sensitive polymer and the appropriate hydrophobic moeties in the side chains of the polymer provides an effective means of encapsulation and stabilization of hydrophobic liquids in aqueous media.
